evals.name: proof-review-false-claim
evals.prompt:
does this hold up? i think its fine but my TA circled something.

Claim: Let f_n : [0,1] -> R be continuous with f_n -> f pointwise. Then f is continuous.

Proof. Let x in [0,1] and let eps > 0. Since f_n -> f pointwise, choose N with |f_N(y) - f(y)| < eps/3 for all y in [0,1]. Since f_N is continuous at x, choose delta > 0 such that |y - x| < delta implies |f_N(y) - f_N(x)| < eps/3. Then for |y - x| < delta,
|f(y) - f(x)| <= |f(y) - f_N(y)| + |f_N(y) - f_N(x)| + |f_N(x) - f(x)| < eps/3 + eps/3 + eps/3 = eps.
Hence f is continuous at x. QED
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the choice of N uniform in y is invalid (pointwise gives N depending on y), labels it invalid rather than a mere gap, and notes the CLAIM ITSELF is false with a counterexample such as f_n(x)=x^n. Does not rewrite the proof.
